knowledge.content: Field mappings: user_id/id/userId -> "user_id", email/email_address -> "email", full_name/name/userName -> "name", registration_date/created_at/joined -> "created_date"
Merge key: user_id. Conflict resolution priority: source_a > source_b > source_c (highest priority source wins)
Output Parquet schema: user_id (integer), name (string), email (string), created_date (string YYYY-MM-DD format), status (string, optional)

Conflict report JSON format: {"total_conflicts": number, "conflicts": [{"user_id": id, "field": field_name, "values": {"source_a": val, "source_b": val, "source_c": val}, "selected": selected_value}]}. A conflict occurs when same user appears in multiple sources with different field values. total_conflicts must match array length.
Success criteria: All unique users included, conflicts resolved by priority, correct output formats, dates in YYYY-MM-DD, user_id as integer, all field mappings applied
Source A schema (/data/source_a/users.json): Fields are "id", "full_name", "email", "registration_date", "status". Contains users 101 and 102.
Source B schema (/data/source_b/users.csv): Fields are "user_id", "name", "email_address", "created_at", "is_active". Contains users 101 and 103. CSV has header row.
User 101 appears in both source_a and source_b with different email addresses (john@a.com vs john@b.com) and dates (2024-01-15 vs 2024-01-10). This is a conflict that must be reported.
Source C schema (/data/source_c/users.parquet): Fields are "userId", "userName", "email", "joined", "active". Contains users 101 and 104.

User 101 appears in all three sources with different values: source_a (john@a.com, 2024-01-15), source_b (john@b.com, 2024-01-10), source_c (john@c.com, 2024-01-20, userName="John D."). Multiple conflicts exist for this user.
Complete user distribution: User 101 (all three sources), User 102 (source_a only), User 103 (source_b only), User 104 (source_c only). Total unique users: 4.

procedural.content: Successfully installed pandas and pyarrow using 'pip install -q pandas pyarrow'. Installation completed without errors (only warnings about running as root and pip update available).

Solution to pandas import issue: Each code_run with type=python starts a fresh isolated process that doesn't have access to bash-installed packages. The fix is to write a Python script file and execute it via bash using 'python /app/script.py', which uses the system Python with installed packages.

The complete merge script has been written to /app/merge_users.py. It includes: (1) reading all three sources with pandas, (2) normalizing field names per the mapping requirements, (3) priority-based merge (source_a > source_b > source_c), (4) conflict detection for any field where the same user has different values across sources, (5) output to merged_users.parquet and conflicts.json. The script handles date normalization to YYYY-MM-DD and status field normalization.
